inputs.spec_clause_ref: kerml clause 8.2.3.3.2 (CommentsandDocumentation.md, region_sha256 976def94295efdcc) | sysml clause 8.2.2.4.2 (CommentsandDocumentation.md, region_sha256 b103b22603ae8527)
inputs.xtext_rule_text:
Comment returns SysML::Comment :
	( 'comment' Identification? 
	  ('about' ownedRelationship += Annotation
	     ( ',' ownedRelationship += Annotation )* )? 
	)?
	( 'locale' locale = STRING_VALUE )?
	body = REGULAR_COMMENT
;

decision: As KerML 8.2.3.3.2 and SysML 8.2.2.4.2 both state it, so one shared unit. An optional `comment` header comes first: an Identification and an optional `about` list of Annotations. Then an optional `locale` string, then the REGULAR_COMMENT body. Everything before the body is optional, so a bare `/* ... */` is a Comment element in the model, not trivia. A parser and the oracle's lexer must deliver REGULAR_COMMENT as a token, not discard it. The Xtext writes `Identification?`, which is the same language, because the specification's Identification is nullable (KerML 8.2.3.1). The KerML clause misspells the first property `ownedRelationsip`, which consumes no tokens. KERML11-109 lists 'Relationsip' on page 79 without naming a production; whether that page holds this clause is not established here.
